resources.title: Architectural curtain planning
resources.subtitle: Geometry, double-height glazing and the cloth envelope
resources.summary: Establish the open view, finished drop and retained cloth before fixing the ceiling or interior layout.

sections.title: Record the opening, then the curtain
items: Give every aperture a reference. Supply a plan, elevation and section with drawing revision, orientation and the source of each dimension. Mark dimensions as design, site-measured or still to be verified.
Record finished floor level, ceiling or track datum, glazing head, sill, doors, handles, opening lights, radiators and furniture. Window height is not the finished curtain drop.

Agree the heading and carrier connection before establishing the curtain top. Set the lower edge against the verified finished floor or sill and the intended clearance or pooling. Do not use a universal deduction.

sections.title: Double-height review
items: Confirm whether the curtain is reachable for operation, dressing and removal. Establish the installation route and future access before the space is furnished.
Record textile width, joins, lining, interlining and heading with the workroom. A small fabric sample cannot establish the behaviour or load of a complete tall curtain.

pages.title: A shaped opening is an operating decision

sections.title: Agree what stays in view
items: Show the proposed track route separately from the glass outline. Identify changing drops and each slope; do not assume symmetry.
Draw the open and closed arrangements. Identify retained upper cloth, tieback positions and the client's required clear view. A shaped curtain need not clear the whole apex when open.
A bent track is not evidence that a motorised curtain can travel on an incline. Agree the arrangement and operating method with Apex and the supplier before specifying a motor.

sections.title: Design review information
items: Share the latest elevation and section, desired open view, privacy and light-control priorities, fabric intentions, floor finish and programme.
Keep provisional geometry separate from an instruction to manufacture. Final survey and coordinated approval must resolve the dimensions and operation.

pages.title: Allow for the cloth as well as the track

sections.title: Fullness, weight and stack-back
items: Fullness describes cloth width relative to the covered width; the required allowance depends on the chosen heading and textile. Confirm it with the workroom rather than applying a universal ratio.

Estimate each textile layer from its cut area and supplier mass per area; include hems, headings, joins and accessories in the completed curtain assessment. Record assumptions and replace the estimate with the agreed made-up weight.
Stack-back is the space occupied along the track when open. Fold depth projects into the room. They are different dimensions and both affect the recess and clear view.
Confirm the stack using the actual heading, layers and fullness. Do not promise a fixed percentage of the window width. Check handles and opening doors in both operating states.

sections.title: Release point
items: Agree the open elevation and stack allowance with the interior designer, then coordinate the track and pocket using APX-T02. Keep the approved textile reference with the aperture record.

resources.title: Tracks, pockets and structural interfaces
resources.subtitle: Coordinate the entire assembly before the ceiling closes
resources.summary: Single and independent double tracks, recessed pockets, mounting arrangements and the information needed to assess support.

sections.title: Build the envelope from the inside out
items: Start with the exact track and carrier, then allow for the selected heading, folds, lining, wall clearance and any projecting handles. Confirm the working envelope in plan and section.

For independent curtain and voile movement, specify two separate operating lines. Record which is nearest the glazing, each draw direction and each stack position. Coordinate motor and power access separately where both are motorised.

Specify and verify independent operation for each curtain and voile layer. Do not infer independent movement from the number of channels in a track profile; confirm the complete arrangement with the supplier.

sections.title: Product drawings before setting the pocket
items: Select the exact Forest track, carrier, bracket and end components before reserving installation space. Obtain their current product drawings and identify the revision used.
A profile drawing alone does not define the complete installation envelope. Confirm cloth movement, bracket projection, drive ends, connections and safe removal with the selected arrangement.
This preliminary edition does not publish profile, recess or cut-out dimensions. Confirm the complete pocket detail individually before the ceiling layout or finishes are released.

sections.title: Ceiling or wall mounted
items: Select the bracket and projection for the whole curtain envelope. Record the supporting construction behind the visible finish and the load path from track to building.
Bracket capacity varies with the component and projection. Do not infer fixing centres, anchor sizes or substrate capacity from a track weight rating. Obtain a project-specific fixing assessment.

sections.title: Recessed track coordination
items: Distinguish a general ceiling pocket from a manufacturer recess extrusion. The pocket must accommodate cloth, brackets, drive ends, assembly and service access, not only the rail.
Obtain the supplier drawing for the exact track generation, heading and drive-end arrangement. Confirm all pocket dimensions, openings, motor orientation and installation access for this project.
A drawing for one straight or curved arrangement is not a universal pocket detail. Agree the finishing sequence with the ceiling contractor and the selected system instructions before concealment.

pages.title: Information needed for a fixing assessment

sections.title: Structural support checklist
items: Identify substrate material, thickness, condition and location; include structural drawings and photographs before concealment. Label evidence with aperture and revision.
Record proposed track length, curtain weight and layers, operation, bracket projection, junctions and the position of motors or concentrated loads.
Identify service zones and penetrations, edge distances and any restrictions on drilling. Confirm who assesses anchors, brackets and supporting structure.
Record backing continuity, accessible fixing zones and the responsible designer's acceptance. A ceiling finish or lining alone is not evidence of suitable support.

sections.title: Hold point before closure
items: Resolve the support and access detail before lining or plaster closes the interface. Keep acceptance and photographs in the existing project workspace.
This guide does not prescribe anchor types, screw sizes, bracket spacing, design loads or structural adequacy. These depend on the actual assembly and building.

resources.title: Motorised tracks and electrical coordination
resources.subtitle: Select the system, then coordinate power, controls and access
resources.summary: A preliminary coordination brief for the curtain specialist, electrical contractor and controls integrator, with official Forest references for product selection.

pages.title: Select a system against the actual curtain

sections.title: Track configuration and load
items: Record the intended track route, overall length, draw direction, joints and curves. Ask Forest to confirm the complete configuration and its suitability for the project.

Confirm the actual made-up curtain weight, heading, lining, friction and expected duty with the proposed motor and track. This edition does not publish motor capacities, track length limits or bend radii.
Published manufacturer limits are reference information for a defined product and configuration. They do not approve the actual installed system or replace a project-specific assessment.
The load assessment includes the track, carriers, brackets, fixings and structure. A motor rating is not approval of the installed assembly.

sections.title: Apex assessment still required
items: Apex supplies the Forest curtain systems covered here. Supply availability does not establish stock, lead time or project suitability. Agree the exact product code, regional variant, current instructions, installation and commissioning responsibilities before procurement.

sections.title: Power is model-specific
items: Identify the exact motor, power supply and control components by product code before planning electrical work. Obtain the current regional instructions from Forest for that combination.

The electrical contractor must confirm the supply, isolation, cable route, protection, connections and any separate power-supply location for the individual project. No electrical ratings or wiring instructions are prescribed in this edition.
Record who supplies, connects, configures and tests each component. Resolve those responsibilities before procurement or installation; a general system description is not an electrical design.

sections.title: Agree the interface with the integrator
items: Record local switching, remote operation, building automation, app use and independent curtain/voile control. Identify who supplies and configures each interface.

Ask Forest and the controls integrator to confirm the required interface and any receiver, adaptor, actuator or third-party equipment for the selected variant. Compatibility must be checked for the complete project configuration.

Record supply position, accessible isolation, cable route, connector access, control protocol and commissioning responsibilities. Keep mains power and low-voltage control connections clearly distinguished.
Refer to the supplied motor manual for switching and power-continuity requirements. Do not use supply interruption as a substitute for a confirmed control command.

sections.title: Confirm the complete installation and removal envelope
items: Motor body dimensions, assembly dimensions and maintenance clearances are different information. This edition withholds numerical motor dimensions and attachment allowances pending supplier clarification.
Obtain a current, product-specific assembly drawing from Forest. Confirm its measurement datums, mounting orientation, drive end, connectors, cable bend space and any separate power supply.

Agree the space needed to fit, connect, rotate or detach the motor and to remove it for service. Confirm the resulting pocket and access openings individually; no standard clearance is prescribed here.
Show the agreed access arrangement on the coordinated project drawings. Keep equipment accessible and obtain acceptance before the ceiling or finishes conceal the installation.

sections.title: Procurement and commissioning hold points
items: Release only after product codes, load, route, mounting, control compatibility and access are confirmed. Agree power-on readiness and limits-setting with the installer.

At handover, record operating limits, control pairing, independent layer operation, isolation location and service access. Attach the actual supplier instructions and serial/product references to the workspace record.

resources.title: Site readiness, installation and maintenance
resources.subtitle: A practical hold-point record for the contractor and project manager
resources.summary: Resolve access, support evidence, protection and commissioning, then preserve a workable route for future maintenance.

sections.title: Contractor readiness record
items: Record project, aperture references, revision, responsible person and proposed installation date. For each item below mark Confirmed / Outstanding / Not applicable, with owner and evidence.
Support: accepted backing/fixing detail and photographs available; hidden services identified; agreed fixing positions accessible.
Dimensions and finishes: final survey agreed; floor and ceiling datums confirmed; wet and dusty work complete; recess and finish match the coordinated detail.
Access: installer has assessed equipment, delivery route, floor conditions and loading, working space, exclusion zones and restrictions. Keep the area clear of furniture and other trades.
Protection and power: protection responsibilities agreed; suitable power and controls ready where required; accessible isolation identified; commissioning attendance booked.

sections.title: Hold point
items: Unresolved support, dimensions, electrical interfaces or safe access must be reviewed before attendance or manufacture is treated as released. Record the decision and responsible person in the workspace.
This checklist supports coordination. It is not a method statement, equipment selection or working-at-height assessment.

sections.title: Installation and commissioning record
items: Confirm smooth full travel and the agreed open/closed positions. Check clearances around cloth, handles, returns and other finishes. For motorised systems, confirm limits and the intended controls with the installer.
Record dressing, outstanding defects, user instruction and completion evidence. Identify who accepts the work and who closes remaining actions.

sections.title: Maintenance and future access
items: Keep a practical route for safe curtain removal, track inspection, drive-end access and motor or power-supply replacement. Record any removable panels and the equipment access strategy.
Issue the care instructions for the actual textile and the manufacturer instructions for the installed track/motor. Do not apply one lubricant or service interval to every product.

Confirm the inspection, servicing and lubrication requirements for the exact installed products with the supplier. Agree who provides ongoing support; this edition sets no universal maintenance interval or lubricant.
Retain product codes, serial numbers, control configuration, isolation position, supplier documents and warranties in the handover record. Reassess access if the room layout or finishes change.
